017package org.apache.juneau.rest.client.jetty;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.io.*;
022import java.nio.channels.*;
023import java.util.concurrent.*;
024
025import org.apache.juneau.rest.client.*;
026import org.eclipse.jetty.client.*;
027import org.eclipse.jetty.util.*;
028
029/**
030 * {@link HttpTransport} implementation backed by Jetty 12 {@link HttpClient}.
031 *
032 * <p>
033 * This transport is auto-discovered via {@link java.util.ServiceLoader} when
034 * {@code org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-client} is on the classpath.  You can also instantiate it explicitly:
035 *
036 * <p class='bjava'>
037 *    <jv>transport</jv> = JettyHttpTransport.<jsm>builder</jsm>()
038 *       .httpClient(<jk>new</jk> HttpClient())
039 *       .build();
040 *
041 *    <jv>client</jv> = RestClient.<jsm>builder</jsm>()
042 *       .transport(<jv>transport</jv>)
043 *       .build();
044 * </p>
045 *
046 * <p>
047 * The Jetty {@link HttpClient} is started automatically when the transport is created and stopped when
048 * {@link #close()} is called.  The request body is streamed via {@link OutputStreamRequestContent} using
049 * a background thread, avoiding full in-memory buffering.  The response header timeout defaults to 30 seconds
050 * and is configurable via {@link JettyHttpTransportBuilder#responseTimeoutMs(long)}.
051 *
052 * <p>
053 * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
054 * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
055 * (and possibly earlier).
056 *
057 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
058 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient">juneau-ng REST client</a>
059 * </ul>
060 *
061 * @since 9.2.1
062 */
063@SuppressWarnings({
064   "resource" // Transport methods return Closeables owned by the caller; Eclipse JDT @Owning warning is by design.
065})
066public final class JettyHttpTransport implements HttpTransport {
067
068   private final HttpClient httpClient;
069   private final long responseTimeoutMs;
070   private final boolean policySupported;
071
072   JettyHttpTransport(JettyHttpTransportBuilder builder) throws Exception {
073      this.policySupported = builder.httpClient == null;
074      this.httpClient = builder.httpClient != null ? builder.httpClient : new CredentialGuardingHttpClient();
075      this.responseTimeoutMs = builder.responseTimeoutMs;
076      if (this.policySupported)
077         // Only a client this transport created (never yet started) reaches here.  Installs a SocketAddressResolver
078         // that pin-on-connects the connections of SSRF-guard-active @Remote requests, which are tagged into a
079         // connection pool of their own (see PolicyPinningSocketAddressResolver); ordinary (non-@Remote)
080         // connections on this same client are completely unaffected. It must be installed
081         // before the client starts, because Jetty rejects a resolver change once started. The default async
082         // resolver is built from the client's executor and scheduler, which are not safely readable until after
083         // start, so the fallback here is Jetty's synchronous SocketAddressResolver.Sync, a supported,
084         // dependency-free implementation, rather than a hand-built copy.
085         this.httpClient.setSocketAddressResolver(new PolicyPinningSocketAddressResolver(new SocketAddressResolver.Sync()));
086      if (!this.httpClient.isStarted())
087         this.httpClient.start();
088   }
089
090   /**
091    * Returns a new builder for this transport.
092    *
093    * @return A new builder. Never <jk>null</jk>.
094    */
095   public static JettyHttpTransportBuilder builder() {
096      return new JettyHttpTransportBuilder();
097   }
098
099   /**
100    * Returns a new instance backed by a default {@link HttpClient}.
101    *
102    * @return A new instance. Never <jk>null</jk>.
103    * @throws Exception If the Jetty {@link HttpClient} cannot be started.
104    */
105   public static JettyHttpTransport create() throws Exception {
106      return builder().build();
107   }
108
109   @Override /* HttpTransport */
110   public TransportResponse execute(TransportRequest request) throws TransportException {
111      if (request.isSsrfGuardActive())
112         return executeWithPolicy(request); // HTT: returns normally only after a pinned connect to a genuinely public address (guarded requests have their own connection pool, so they never reuse an unpinned connection), which a hermetic loopback test cannot make
113      try {
114         return sendOnce(request);
115      } catch (StaleConnectionException e) {
116         // A pooled keep-alive connection was torn down by the server before any response was received.
117         // Replay once on a fresh connection, but only when it is provably safe (idempotent + repeatable body).
118         if (! request.isSafeToReplay())
119            throw e.asTransportException();
120         try {
121            return sendOnce(request);
122         } catch (StaleConnectionException e2) {
123            throw e2.asTransportException();
124         }
125      }
126   }
127
128   @Override /* HttpTransport */
129   public boolean supportsUrlPolicy() {
130      return policySupported;
131   }
132
133   // Juneau-controlled redirect revalidation for a guarded request; every hop is pinned (see buildJettyRequest).
134   private TransportResponse executeWithPolicy(TransportRequest request) throws TransportException {
135      return PolicyEnforcedRedirects.execute(request, this::sendOncePinned); // HTT: same as above; returns normally only after a pinned connect to a public address
136   }
137
138   // Performs one pin-on-connect hop: the hop request is still SSRF-guard-active, so it is tagged into the pinned
139   // connection pool.  Jetty's own redirect-following is disabled so PolicyEnforcedRedirects owns the loop.
140   private TransportResponse sendOncePinned(TransportRequest request) throws TransportException {
141      try {
142         return sendOnce(request, false); // HTT: same as above; completes only after a pinned connect to a public address
143      } catch (StaleConnectionException e) { // HTT: needs a pooled connection in the pinned pool that the server then drops, and every connection in that pool was pinned to a public address, which a hermetic loopback test cannot reach
144         throw e.asTransportException(); // HTT: see the catch above
145      }
146   }
147
148   // Performs a single HTTP exchange.  Throws StaleConnectionException (a retryable signal) when the failure is a
149   // pre-response stale-connection failure; throws TransportException for every other failure.
150   private TransportResponse sendOnce(TransportRequest request) throws TransportException, StaleConnectionException {
151      return sendOnce(request, true);
152   }
153
154   private TransportResponse sendOnce(TransportRequest request, boolean followRedirects) throws TransportException, StaleConnectionException {
155      var jettyRequest = buildJettyRequest(request).followRedirects(followRedirects);
156      var listener = new InputStreamResponseListener();
157      jettyRequest.send(listener);
158      Response jettyResponse;
159      try {
160         // A per-request timeout overrides the transport-level response header timeout.
161         var perRequest = request.getTimeout();
162         long waitMs;
163         if (perRequest != null)
164            waitMs = Math.max(1, perRequest.toMillis());
165         else if (responseTimeoutMs > 0)
166            waitMs = responseTimeoutMs;
167         else
168            waitMs = Long.MAX_VALUE;
169         jettyResponse = listener.get(waitMs, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
170      } catch (InterruptedException e) {
171         Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
172         abortQuietly(listener);
173         throw new TransportException("HTTP request interrupted", e);
174      } catch (TimeoutException e) {
175         abortQuietly(listener);
176         throw new TransportException("HTTP request timed out", e);
177      } catch (ExecutionException e) {
178         abortQuietly(listener);
179         var cause = e.getCause();
180         if (isStaleConnectionFailure(cause))
181            throw new StaleConnectionException(cause);
182         throw new TransportException("HTTP transport error: " + cause.getMessage(), cause);
183      }
184      return buildTransportResponse(jettyResponse, listener.getInputStream());
185   }
186
187   // A failure is a stale-connection (pre-response) failure when the server closed the pooled connection before
188   // sending any response.  Jetty surfaces this as an end-of-file exception (Jetty's EofException is a subclass)
189   // or a closed-channel exception.  Because the response listener only returns once response headers have
190   // arrived, any such failure here is guaranteed to have occurred before any response bytes were read.
191   private static boolean isStaleConnectionFailure(Throwable cause) {
192      return cause instanceof EOFException || cause instanceof ClosedChannelException;
193   }
194
195   // Releases the Jetty response content when the response never reaches the caller (interrupt/timeout/error),
196   // so the connection is not abandoned.  Closing the listener's input stream aborts and releases the exchange.
197   private static void abortQuietly(InputStreamResponseListener listener) {
198      try {
199         listener.getInputStream().close();
200      } catch (IOException e) { // HTT: InputStreamResponseListener's input stream close() never throws IOException in practice; the catch only satisfies the declared signature
201         // Best-effort cleanup on an already-failing path; nothing more can be done.
202      }
203   }
204
205   @Override /* Closeable */
206   public void close() throws IOException {
207      try {
208         httpClient.stop();
209      } catch (Exception e) {
210         throw ioex(e, "Failed to stop Jetty HttpClient: %s", e.getMessage());
211      }
212   }
213
214   // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
215   // Internal helpers
216   // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
217
218   private Request buildJettyRequest(TransportRequest request) throws TransportException {
219      Request jettyRequest;
220      try {
221         // A client this transport created strips credential headers from every redirect copy itself; a caller-supplied
222         // client is left unchanged, so its requests are created as CredentialGuardingHttpRequest, which strips them from
223         // its own copies.  That is what HttpClient.newRequest(URI) builds too, but in a guarded subclass: Jetty copies a
224         // request for a redirect with the request's own copy(URI), and does not carry its listeners or attributes over,
225         // so the guard cannot be attached to whatever a client's newRequest returns.  An override of
226         // newRequest(URI) on a caller-supplied client is therefore not called; see JettyHttpTransportBuilder.httpClient.
227         jettyRequest = (policySupported ? httpClient.newRequest(request.getUri()) : new CredentialGuardingHttpRequest(httpClient, request.getUri()))
228            .method(request.getMethod());
229      } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
230         // Jetty refuses a URI that java.net.URI parsed with a null host (for example an underscore host name).
231         throw new TransportException("HTTP transport error: " + e.getMessage(), e);
232      }
233      // The tag is part of Jetty's destination key, so a guarded request gets a connection pool of its own whose
234      // connections are all opened through the pin; it can never reuse a connection an unguarded request opened.
235      if (request.isSsrfGuardActive())
236         jettyRequest.tag(PolicyPinningSocketAddressResolver.tagFor(request.getAllowedAddressRanges()));
237      for (var h : request.getHeaders())
238         jettyRequest.headers(fields -> fields.add(h.name(), h.value()));
239      var body = request.getBody();
240      if (body != null)
241         jettyRequest.body(buildRequestContent(body));
242      return jettyRequest;
243   }
244
245   private static OutputStreamRequestContent buildRequestContent(TransportBody body) {
246      var ct = body.getContentType();
247      var contentType = ct != null ? ct : "application/octet-stream";
248      var content = new OutputStreamRequestContent(contentType);
249      // Write body to the content's OutputStream on a background thread so Jetty can stream it concurrently.
250      var writer = new Thread(() -> {
251         try (var out = content.getOutputStream()) {
252            body.writeTo(out);
253         } catch (IOException e) {
254            // Closing the stream on error signals Jetty to abort the request.
255         }
256      }, "juneau-ng-body-writer");
257      writer.setDaemon(true);
258      writer.start();
259      return content;
260   }
261
262   private static TransportResponse buildTransportResponse(Response jettyResponse, InputStream bodyStream) {
263      var builder = TransportResponse.builder()
264         .statusCode(jettyResponse.getStatus())
265         .reasonPhrase(jettyResponse.getReason())
266         .body(bodyStream)
267         // Release the Jetty response InputStream when the RestResponse is closed; TransportResponse.close() only runs this callback.
268         .closeCallback(bodyStream);
269      jettyResponse.getHeaders().forEach(field -> builder.header(field.getName(), field.getValue()));
270      return builder.build();
271   }
272
273   // Internal signal that a pre-response stale-connection failure occurred and may be retried once.  Carries the
274   // original cause so the caller can build the user-visible TransportException if the retry is not attempted or
275   // also fails.
276   private static final class StaleConnectionException extends Exception {
277      private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
278
279      StaleConnectionException(Throwable cause) {
280         super(cause);
281      }
282
283      TransportException asTransportException() {
284         return new TransportException("HTTP transport error: " + getCause().getMessage(), getCause());
285      }
286   }
287}
